title: Ansel and the Ledger
premise: In 1848, Silas Montrose, a woman disguised as a male apprentice clockmaker to keep her dead father's trade, is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock in a city sliding into revolution. Inside she discovers the clock's hidden ledger—a record of debts, bribes, and disappearances kept by the observatory's director—and a child abandoned at her door with instructions to forget his face. As the uprising burns the archives and the victors begin rewriting history, Silas must decide whether survival means silence. She smuggles the ledger and the boy out through the collapsing city, publishes the truth at the cost of her workshop, and ends the book years later as the boy, grown, reads her name aloud from the restored record—proof that memory outlives power.
about_author: Marguerite Sandoval is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing seized documents from failed nineteenth-century uprisings. She writes historical fiction about the people history almost forgot, from a farmhouse full of clocks.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Silas Montrose, passing as a man to keep her father's clockmaking shop, is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock. In the tower she notices the mechanism has been deliberately slowed—and that someone winds a second, secret movement inside the case. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: cautious pride curdling into unease.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: A boy of seven is left at Silas's shop at night with a note: forget his face. She cannot. The child clutches a brass key stamped with the observatory's mark. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness against the instinct to stay invisible and safe.

chapters.title: The Second Movement
chapters.summary: Silas returns to the observatory with the boy's key and finds the hidden ledger: names of the disappeared, payments, orders signed by Director Havel. The director catches her, offers her a fortune to forget what gears she has seen. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: fear and the first taste of complicity refused.

chapters.title: What the City Remembers
chapters.summary: Revolution ignites in the streets below. Silas's neighbor, a printer named Okafor, shows her pamphlets already rewriting the uprising's causes—victors' history being printed before the fighting ends. The boy, Tam, begins to speak of the face he was told to forget. POV: Silas, with an Okafor interlude. Emotional beat: the theme of memory sharpening into urgency.

chapters.title: Orders Come
chapters.summary: Havel's men search the clockmakers' quarter, confiscating tools and records. Silas hides Tam and the ledger inside a grandfather clock she is 'delivering.' Her apprentice, Jem, is arrested in her place. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: guilt—the cost of measuring the world in what can be carried.

chapters.title: The Bargain of Belonging
chapters.summary: Silas trades a repaired chronometer for Jem's release, but Havel demands the ledger in return and reveals he knows she is a woman. Belonging, she realizes, has always been a transaction she never set the terms of. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: humiliation transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Burning the Archive
chapters.summary: The mob fires the observatory's records hall. Silas and Okafor race the flames to copy the ledger's pages; Tam, who recognizes Havel as the man who took his parents, insists on coming. POV: Silas, shifting briefly to Tam. Emotional beat: terror and fierce, fragile trust.

chapters.title: Every Clock in the City
chapters.summary: Havel seizes the shop and declares Silas dead in the riots. She and Tam hide in the clock tower itself, repairing the sabotaged master clock so every church bell in the city strikes the true hour at the moment her testimony is read aloud in the square. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the plan crystallizing—time itself as witness.

chapters.title: The Hour of Record
chapters.summary: Climax. At the unified stroke of noon, Okafor reads the ledger from the printing-house steps as every clock in the city confirms the hour. Havel's men close in; Tam steps forward and names his parents' faces before the crowd. Havel falls not to violence but to a city that now remembers. POV: Silas, then Tam. Emotional beat: terror breaking into triumph.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Years later, Silas—her identity open, her shop rebuilt with Tam as her apprentice—attends the restoration of the observatory clock. The ledger enters the official archive with her name on the record. Tam, grown, reads the dedication aloud. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet belonging, finally unearned by disguise—memory outlasting power.
